data.text: The evidence is consistent: the outage began with a modem sync loss, the modem has since re‑registered and is operational, the WAN NIC is up and the gateway still answers ARP — yet traffic through it fails, and the watchdog itself flagged a WAN reload as the correct action while sitting in observe mode.

data.reason: The cable modem dropped sync (~02:01, T3 timeout), failed to fetch its config (TFTP file NOT FOUND) and rebooted/re-registered at ~02:28; the firewall's WAN interface still holds the pre-reboot lease (198.51.100.27) and was never renewed, so its addressing no longer matches what the provider path serves, leaving the internet down even though the modem is now OPERATIONAL.

data.cause: The cable modem dropped sync (~02:01, T3 timeout), failed to fetch its config (TFTP file NOT FOUND) and rebooted/re-registered at ~02:28; the firewall's WAN interface still holds the pre-reboot lease (198.51.100.27) and was never renewed, so its addressing no longer matches what the provider path serves, leaving the internet down even though the modem is now OPERATIONAL.
evidence: Modem events show the outage origin: 'No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out' at 02:01:44, 'TFTP failed - configuration file NOT FOUND' at 02:14:10, then 'Cable Modem Reboot because of - unknown; registration complete' at 02:28:21 (cat /var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl).

Modem metrics show NOT_SYNCHRONIZED at 02:06, then OPERATIONAL from 02:29 onward with healthy SNR (min_snr 37.6-37.9 dB), i.e. the modem itself recovered (tail /var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-metrics.jsonl).

Watchdog decisions: action 'none' while modem not operational/settling, then action 'reload' at 02:30 (reason modem_operational, down_seconds 1440), but only 'would_reload' was recorded — mode is observe, so no renewal actually happened (tail /var/db/wan-watchdog/events.jsonl; state.json shows last_action reload, reloads_in_outage 2).
WAN link and L2 path are fine: vtnet0 is UP,RUNNING,LOWER_UP, status active with inet 198.51.100.27 (ifconfig vtnet0), and the gateway has a live ARP entry 00:17:10:9a:a3:96 (arp -a).
Yet the gateway does not respond: 'ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1' shows 3 transmitted, 0 received, 100% packet loss — traffic beyond L2 is dead despite an active link.

The lease on file predates the modem reboot and is well within its lifetime (renew 2026/3/5, expire 2026/3/6), so dhclient had no reason to renew it during the outage (cat /var/db/dhclient.leases.vtnet0).
data.recommendation: Renew the WAN DHCP lease on gw.lan (release/re-acquire on vtnet0) now that the modem is re-registered and OPERATIONAL; that is exactly the reload the watchdog's own logic selected at 02:30 but could not apply in observe mode. Longer term, consider letting the watchdog act automatically after the modem-settling window, and have the maintainer ask the ISP about the plant errors behind the sync loss (rising uncorrected codewords, TFTP config file NOT FOUND).
data.detail: Stale WAN DHCP lease after modem re-registration; WAN never re-dialed
